import re

# Supported format strings tried in order
_FORMATS = [

    "%d/%m/%Y",       # 15/03/2024
    "%m-%d-%Y",       # 03-15-2024
    "%m/%d/%Y",       # 03/15/2024
    "%B %d, %Y",      # March 15, 2024

    "%d.%m.%Y",       # 15.03.2024

    "%b, %d, %Y",     # Mar, 15, 2024
    "%Y %m %d",       # 2024 03 15
    "%d %m %Y",       # 15 03 2024
]


def parse_date(s: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """Parse a date string and return (year, month, day).

    Supports a wide range of common formats such as:
      - ISO format:        2024-03-15
      - Slash-separated:   2024/03/15, 03/15/2024, 15/03/2024
      - Long month name:   March 15, 2024
      - Short month name:  Mar 15, 2024
      - Dot-separated:     2024.03.15

    Raises ValueError if the string cannot be parsed as a date.
    """
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected a string, got {type(s).__name__!r}")

    s = s.strip()
    if not s:
        raise ValueError("Empty date string")

    for fmt in _FORMATS:
        try:
            dt = datetime.strptime(s, fmt)
            return (dt.year, dt.month, dt.day)
        except ValueError:
            continue

    raise ValueError(f"Cannot parse date string: {s!r}")

def _normalize(s: str) -> str:
    """Normalize whitespace and common punctuation variants."""
    # collapse multiple spaces
    s = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s)
    # Remove ordinal suffixes: 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, etc.
    s = re.sub(r'(\d+)(st|nd|rd|th)\b', r'\1', s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    return s.strip()


def parse_date(s: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """Parse a date string and return (year, month, day).

    Supports a wide range of common formats such as:
      - ISO format:        2024-03-15
      - Slash-separated:   2024/03/15, 03/15/2024, 15/03/2024
      - Long month name:   March 15, 2024
      - Short month name:  Mar 15, 2024
      - Dot-separated:     2024.03.15
      - Ordinal:           March 1st, 2024

    Raises ValueError if the string cannot be parsed as a date.
    """
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected a string, got {type(s).__name__!r}")

    s = s.strip()
    if not s:
        raise ValueError("Empty date string")

    normalized = _normalize(s)

    for candidate in [normalized, normalized.title()]:
        for fmt in _FORMATS:
            try:
                dt = datetime.strptime(candidate, fmt)
                return (dt.year, dt.month, dt.day)
            except ValueError:
                continue

    raise ValueError(f"Cannot parse date string: {s!r}")

import re
from datetime import datetime


# Supported format strings tried in order
_FORMATS = [
    "%Y-%m-%d",       # 2024-03-15
    "%Y/%m/%d",       # 2024/03/15
    "%m-%d-%Y",       # 03-15-2024
    "%m/%d/%Y",       # 03/15/2024

    "%B %d %Y",       # March 15 2024
    "%b %d %Y",       # Mar 15 2024
    "%d %B %Y",       # 15 March 2024
    "%d %b %Y",       # 15 Mar 2024
    "%Y.%m.%d",       # 2024.03.15
    "%d.%m.%Y",       # 15.03.2024
    "%m.%d.%Y",       # 03.15.2024
    "%B, %d, %Y",     # March, 15, 2024
    "%b, %d, %Y",     # Mar, 15, 2024
    "%Y %m %d",       # 2024 03 15
    "%d %m %Y",       # 15 03 2024
    "%d-%B-%Y",       # 15-March-2024
    "%d-%b-%Y",       # 15-Mar-2024
    "%d/%B/%Y",       # 15/March/2024
    "%d/%b/%Y",       # 15/Mar/2024
    "%Y-%b-%d",       # 2024-Mar-15
    "%Y-%B-%d",       # 2024-March-15
    # Two-digit year variants
    "%d/%m/%y",       # 15/03/24
    "%m/%d/%y",       # 03/15/24
    "%y-%m-%d",       # 24-03-15
    # Additional formats
    "%B %d %Y",       # March 15 2024
    "%d %B, %Y",      # 15 March, 2024
    "%Y, %B %d",      # 2024, March 15
    "%d. %B %Y",      # 15. March 2024
    "%d. %b %Y",      # 15. Mar 2024
    "%B-%d-%Y",       # March-15-2024
    "%b-%d-%Y",       # Mar-15-2024
    "%m-%d-%y",       # 03-15-24
    "%d-%m-%y",       # 15-03-24
    "%Y%m%d",         # 20240315
]


def _normalize(s: str) -> str:
    """Normalize whitespace and common punctuation variants."""
    # collapse multiple spaces
    s = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s)
    # Remove ordinal suffixes: 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, etc.
    s = re.sub(r'(\d+)(st|nd|rd|th)\b', r'\1', s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    return s.strip()


def _try_parse(candidate: str) -> tuple[int, int, int] | None:
    """Try all formats against the candidate string. Return tuple or None."""
    for fmt in _FORMATS:
        try:
            dt = datetime.strptime(candidate, fmt)
            return (dt.year, dt.month, dt.day)
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return None


def parse_date(s: str) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """Parse a date string and return (year, month, day).

    Supports a wide range of common formats such as:
      - ISO format:        2024-03-15
      - Slash-separated:   2024/03/15, 03/15/2024, 15/03/2024
      - Long month name:   March 15, 2024
      - Short month name:  Mar 15, 2024
      - Dot-separated:     2024.03.15
      - Ordinal:           March 1st, 2024

    Raises ValueError if the string cannot be parsed as a date.
    """
    if not isinstance(s, str):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected a string, got {type(s).__name__!r}")

    s = s.strip()
    if not s:
        raise ValueError("Empty date string")

    normalized = _normalize(s)

    # Try various capitalizations
    candidates = [
        normalized,
        normalized.title(),
        normalized.capitalize(),
        normalized.upper(),
        normalized.lower(),
    ]
    
    # Also try replacing commas followed by non-space with comma-space
    extra = re.sub(r',(\S)', r', \1', normalized)
    if extra != normalized:
        candidates.append(extra)
        candidates.append(extra.title())

    # Try replacing dots used as separators with dashes
    dot_to_dash = re.sub(r'(\d)\.(\d)', r'\1-\2', normalized)
    if dot_to_dash != normalized:
        candidates.append(dot_to_dash)

    seen = set()
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(candidate)
        result = _try_parse(candidate)
        if result is not None:
            return result

    raise ValueError(f"Cannot parse date string: {s!r}")
